title: Reviewer Finding Report
description: The canonical wire contract every reviewer subagent EMITS to the primary agent (review-report-standards Rendering 2). The primary agent parses it to merge the swarm, compute the merged verdict, and track fixes across rounds. This file defines the SHAPE and value domains only; the SEMANTICS (severity anchoring, verdict arithmetic, ID stability, status lifecycle, the human rendering) live in the review-report-standards skill. Emit MINIFIED JSON conforming to this schema.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Pinned so a consumer can detect a shape change.

target.description: Files/dirs reviewed. Always a list, consistent with a finding's locations.

generated.description: ISO 8601 date only (no wall-clock time), taken from the date provided in context.

speculative.description: Concerns that failed the Realism test (review-core, Realism test); not findings. May be empty. Counting rule: review-report-standards, Verdict Arithmetic.

conventions_profile.description: OPTIONAL. A reusable summary of this codebase's own conventions. Which reviewers use this field, and its reuse behavior, are owned by review-report-standards.

plan_revision.description: OPTIONAL. Used only by lens-test-quality-reviewer on a flow-testing dispatch: the full test-plan body plus reviewer (PLAN-CHALLENGE mode) or amendments (TESTS mode, or a trim re-challenge), which the orchestrator writes unchanged to a fields-file. Its shape is test-plan.schema.json's and is validated by the flow-testing scripts (test-plan-challenge.sh / test-plan-amend.sh), never by this schema — hence an open object here.

volume.description: OPTIONAL. Used only by lens-test-quality-reviewer in flow-testing TESTS mode: its one-line volume verdict on the authored tests.

id.description: Stable, reviewer-prefixed identifier; ID stability (assignment/reuse/renumbering) is owned by review-report-standards. PREFIX = the reviewer's own declared tag (non-exhaustive examples: CLEAN, DOC, SEC, TEST, CONS, OBS, PERF, COMPAT, PERS; tech reviewers use their distinguishing word, e.g. RUST, JAVA, KOTLIN, PHP, REACT, PYTHON, SHELL, DEVOPS, CLOUDFLARE) — see review-report-standards for the derivation rule; each reviewer's own body is authoritative.

realism.description: review-core, Realism test. Counting rule: review-report-standards, Verdict Arithmetic.

trigger.description: ONE line: the concrete real-use scenario that makes the problem happen (review-core, Realism test).

realism_reason.description: OPTIONAL. ONE line of at most 100 characters: why the finding is classed edge-case (review-core, Realism test). No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

category.description: Sub-lens tag from the reviewer's OWN controlled vocabulary (not free text). The closed per-reviewer value set is owned by each reviewer agent; their union, each category flagged security or not, is contracts/review-category.schema.json, and the flow-review writers reject a category outside it. A category flagged security in contracts/review-category.schema.json (x-categories) puts the item under the security floor: proof alone, never unproven (writer-enforced); the floor stays on a finding whose stored or updated category is a security one. An item whose text names a security weakness listed in x-security-terms (a finding's problem or trigger, a speculative entry's concern) takes one of the reviewer's own security categories; a reviewer with none passes it to lens-security-reviewer as a handoff (writer-enforced).

locations.description: One or more `file:line` (or `file:start-end`) sites. An array because a finding may span sites (e.g. duplication). A site outside the diff needs its own entry's relates_to on a changed line. On a flow-testing dispatch, lens-test-quality-reviewer may also use `plan:<item>` locators naming a test-plan entry (e.g. `plan:test-3`).

relates_to.description: OPTIONAL. ONE `file:line` (or `file:start-end`) location of at most 300 characters, on a line the diff changed (diff-scope.sh's diff-hunks.tsv): the changed code that relies on or exposes a defect located outside the diff. A location outside the diff is accepted only when its own entry's relates_to is on a changed line, and a relates_to given always is (writer-enforced at write time). No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

proof.description: OPTIONAL in this shape; writer-enforced: an edge-case finding carries exactly one of proof or unproven, and under the security floor (reviewer lens-security-reviewer, or a security category) proof alone — a security concern stays realistic until proven harmless. ONE line of at most 100 characters: the evidence that the item is rare or harmless. A proof names its evidence as a file:line locator whose file is path-like — it holds a letter and has an extension, a "/", or is Makefile, Dockerfile, Justfile, Rakefile, Gemfile or Procfile — and is no part of a URL (src/a.rs:42, src/a.rs:42-50, Makefile:3; never 10:30), naming a regular file under the writer's --repo-root and a line within it (writer-enforced), or in a test-plan review (plan_review) also a test number the reviewed plan holds (test 3; resolved against the writer's --plan). A reviewer has no shell, so a proof starting "ran " (a command and its result) is recorded only by the orchestrator (review-update-status.sh --proof or --resolution-proof). No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

unproven.description: OPTIONAL in this shape; writer-enforced as for proof, which it excludes: the item is set aside without proof. Only the value true is written.

resolution_proof.description: OPTIONAL in this shape; writer-enforced: required when the entry sets status RESOLVED on a finding not already RESOLVED, and given only with status RESOLVED. ONE line of at most 100 characters: the evidence the fix holds, in the proof form of proof. No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

first_seen.description: ISO 8601 date only, frozen at creation; kept unchanged across rounds.

problem.description: ONE line: what is wrong. Never restate large code.

fix.description: ONE line: the concrete remedy the implementer should apply.

location.description: One `file:line` (or `file:start-end`) site — the same locator form as a finding's locations.

concern.description: ONE line: the concern as the reviewer would have raised it.

why_speculative.description: ONE line: what the concern would need that is not in evidence (review-core, Realism test).

category.description: The reviewer's category for the concern, from its own controlled vocabulary, as for a finding (contracts/review-category.schema.json; writer-enforced). A category flagged security in contracts/review-category.schema.json (x-categories) puts the item under the security floor: proof alone, never unproven (writer-enforced); the floor stays on a finding whose stored or updated category is a security one. An item whose text names a security weakness listed in x-security-terms (a finding's problem or trigger, a speculative entry's concern) takes one of the reviewer's own security categories; a reviewer with none passes it to lens-security-reviewer as a handoff (writer-enforced).

real_if.description: OPTIONAL. ONE line of at most 100 characters: the evidence that would make the concern real (review-core, Realism test). No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

relates_to.description: OPTIONAL. ONE `file:line` (or `file:start-end`) location of at most 300 characters, on a line the diff changed (diff-scope.sh's diff-hunks.tsv): the changed code that relies on or exposes a defect located outside the diff. A location outside the diff is accepted only when its own entry's relates_to is on a changed line, and a relates_to given always is (writer-enforced at write time). No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

proof.description: OPTIONAL in this shape; writer-enforced: every speculative entry carries exactly one of proof or unproven, and under the security floor (reviewer lens-security-reviewer, or a security category) proof alone — a security concern stays realistic until proven harmless. ONE line of at most 100 characters: the evidence that the item is not real or harmless, in the proof form of a finding's proof. No invisible format character (bidi, zero-width, soft hyphen, variation selector, BOM, tag): `not` covers the BMP ones; the flow-review scripts also reject tag characters and supplementary variation selectors.

unproven.description: OPTIONAL in this shape; writer-enforced as for proof, which it excludes: the item is set aside without proof. Only the value true is written.

findings.trigger: this change adds a field to OrderDto and had to repeat the mapping edit in all three sites
findings.problem: dto->entity mapping duplicated across 3 sites; edits must be made in parallel
findings.fix: extract map_order(); call from all three

speculative.concern: OrderService may grow a second responsibility if refunds are added
speculative.why_speculative: no refund work is in the diff or planned; the service has one job today
speculative.real_if: refund handling is added to OrderService

findings.trigger: a release tag containing a newline is passed as --tag; tags come from the team's own CI, which never emits one
findings.realism_reason: tags come only from the team's own CI, which never emits a newline
findings.proof: .github/workflows/release.yml:12 builds the tag from the semver
findings.problem: the tag is read with a line-based read, so an embedded newline truncates it
findings.fix: reject a --tag containing a newline before it reaches the read
